response:
Diagnosis. The archive now has a clear structure. (1) The best single quality channel is refinancing pressure, dlc/act: Standardized Profit Less Rollover Risk leads on both dimensions (fmb 2.90, alpha 3.5%, t 3.26, Sharpe 0.30). (2) The industry-demeaned twin *raised* the FMB slope (3.27) but *lowered* alpha and Sharpe (2.8%, 0.19), which means the within-industry component carries the cross-sectional slope while the across-industry component carries portfolio alpha — a hybrid standardization is the untested implication. (3) The erosion×claims term is the largest-|alpha| object in the archive (−6.6%, t −3.79) but has essentially no linear cross-sectional slope (−0.15), and its additive decomposition was weaker in alpha (−3.1%), confirming the payoff needs multiplicative co-occurrence; the right repair is to use it as a *bounded conditioning weight*, which is exactly the structure that worked in Health Weighted Profitability (alpha 3.5%, Sharpe 0.28). (4) Channels that failed cleanly and should not be revisited: MIN conjunctions (three failures), five-year trends and counts, working-capital intensity, own-history leverage creep. This batch consolidates on the two productive channels through structures that have demonstrated they convert alpha into slope, tests one anatomy question (what in dlc/act matters), and opens one new quality channel (earnings-cash conversion as a conditioner).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion
EXPRESSION: SUB(SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Refinancing pressure and margin erosion are economically distinct fragility routes — one is a funding-market risk, the other a franchise-decay risk — so subtracting both from operating profitability should identify durable strength more sharply than removing either alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two penalty channels are the archive's best-performing quality legs and are unlikely to be redundant (a cash-rich firm with a decaying franchise has no rollover risk, and an inventory-heavy grower at its own margin peak has no erosion), so their combination tests whether the leader's alpha and the erosion signal's alpha are additive. All three legs are winsorized and standardized to unit dispersion, so no term can dominate the sort by scale, which is what made the earlier unstandardized versions degenerate.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Erosion Weighted Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MUL(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5), RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Current profitability deserves credit only from firms that have not been losing margin against fixed obligations; the franchise-decay state should scale the profitability premium rather than be netted against it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the targeted repair of the archive's largest-alpha but zero-slope signal: mapping levered erosion into a bounded [0,1] rank weight removes its extreme skew (the cause of the flat FMB slope) while preserving its portfolio-relevant ordering, and the same weighting structure already delivered 3.5% alpha with a 2.34 FMB t-stat when applied to rollover risk. If it beats both parents, conditional weighting rather than standardized differencing becomes the preferred structure for the remaining generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Profit Less Maturity Concentration
EXPRESSION: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: What makes near-term debt dangerous for a profitable firm is the concentration of claims falling due relative to all claims — a maturity-structure choice — rather than merely the thinness of liquid assets available to repay it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a one-input anatomy test of the current leader that distinguishes two economically different readings of dlc/act: liquidity backing versus maturity concentration; because lt is the denominator the leg is scale-free, defined for nearly all firms, and orthogonal to inventory-cycle differences that drive act. The result tells us whether future refinements should push toward liquidity measures or toward debt-structure measures, which is a decision the archive cannot currently make.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Attainable margins are technology- and industry-determined, so profitability should be judged against industry peers, whereas refinancing pressure is priced by capital markets on an absolute basis and its cross-industry variation is genuine risk information rather than a nuisance sector tilt.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-3 pair showed that demeaning both legs raised the FMB slope (2.90→3.27) but cut alpha (3.5%→2.8%) and Sharpe (0.30→0.19), which implies the informative demeaning is on the profitability leg while the fragility leg's absolute level carries the abnormal return. This asymmetric standardization is the direct implication of that evidence and should, if the diagnosis is right, dominate both parents on slope and alpha simultaneously.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(ADD(xint, dlc), at)), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profit that exceeds committed claims is only credible if it arrives as cash: accrual-inflated earnings cannot service interest or repay maturing debt, so the coverage spread should be weighted by the degree to which reported income is cash-backed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This opens the earnings-quality channel that the archive has never tested, but does so as a bounded conditioner on the solvency-adjusted profit spread rather than as an additive accruals leg, so it cannot collapse into the Sloan sort — a firm with pristine cash conversion but no coverage still scores near zero. The mechanism is a genuine interaction: cash conversion matters precisely because the claims are contractual and must be paid in cash.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Persistent Profit Less Persistent Rollover
EXPRESSION: SUB(ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MA(RATIO(dlc, act), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Both operating strength and funding fragility are structural states rather than one-year snapshots, so three-year averages of margin and of refinancing pressure should identify durable strength better than the latest fiscal year, whose short-term debt balance is partly a timing accident.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The economic story emphasizes persistence, and this isolates exactly the smoothing choice on the leader while leaving its channels and standardization untouched — a cheap and decisive test of whether the leader's power comes from a durable state or from transient fiscal-year positioning. Averaging should also stabilize portfolio composition and raise Sharpe if turnover in the extreme deciles is currently noise-driven.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Profit Less Rollover Less Erosion---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent and correctly scaled, but it is a mechanical third-leg stack of two archive legs — and the erosion leg's near-zero FMB slope (-0.15) makes it likely to dilute the leader's cross-sectional t-stat while adding little independent alpha, so the informational payoff is modest.

---CRITIQUE Erosion Weighted Profitability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible re-shaping of the skewed erosion leg into a bounded conditioner, but the structure inherits a real sign pathology already latent in Health Weighted Profitability — multiplying a signed z-score by a positive rank weight means unprofitable firms are penalized *more* for having low erosion — so any result will be hard to interpret as evidence for the stated conditional mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Profit Less Maturity Concentration---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is only a denominator swap on one leg of the leader, but act→lt changes the leg's economic content from liquidity backing to maturity concentration and yields a diagnostic the archive genuinely cannot currently resolve, so it is a legitimate if narrow anatomy test.

---CRITIQUE Industry Profit Less Absolute Rollover Risk---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The asymmetric demeaning is the correct and specific implication of the observed slope-up/alpha-down divergence between the two gen-3 parents, the expected sign matches the expression's natural direction, and the test cleanly separates which leg's cross-industry variation is priced versus nuisance.

---CRITIQUE Cash Conversion Weighted Coverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: It opens a genuinely untested earnings-quality channel and is not a bare accruals sort, but (ib − oancf)/at is exactly the Sloan cash-flow accrual measure so part of any result will be the known accruals premium, and the signed-z-score × positive-rank construction again perversely rewards weak cash conversion among negative-coverage firms; oancf availability may also cut coverage.

---CRITIQUE Persistent Profit Less Persistent Rollover---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a pure smoothing-window knob on the existing leader with no new economic content — precisely the cosmetic parameter variant the objective warns against — and three-year averaging of annual accounting ratios is very likely to produce a near-collinear signal rather than a diagnostic about durability.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Supplier Financed Profit Discount
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), act), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating profitability that rests on heavy non-debt operating liabilities — stretched payables and accrued expenses funding the working-capital cycle — is lower quality than the same margin earned with self-funded working capital, because operating-liability leverage inflates returns on invested capital while creating claims that tighten precisely when trade creditors reassess the firm.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This drops the smoothing-knob idea and instead opens a quality channel the archive has never touched: fragility from *operating* liabilities rather than from financial debt, maturity structure, franchise erosion, or accruals, so it is informative regardless of outcome and should be largely orthogonal to the dlc-based legs already tested. It uses the bounded-rank conditioning structure that has produced the archive's best joint results (Health Weighted Profitability: alpha 3.5%, Sharpe 0.28), and all inputs are broadly reported so coverage should hold at the archive norm.
